newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S.-Korean firm to begin Panama resort in May.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Korean firm to begin Panama resort in May.

text.p: A U.S.-Korean consortium will begin construction in May of a $300 million resort complex on a former U.S. military base in Panama, a government spokeswoman said Friday.

United Enterprise Trust Group will begin the first stage of construction of a 12-story, 500-room luxury hotel on an island off Fort Amador, a former U.S. World War II nerve center, a Regional Interoceanic Authority (ARI) spokeswoman said.
ARI is the government body in charge of attracting investment on military installations in Panama to be vacated by the United States, in accordance with bilateral treaties.
The company will also build a monorail system, a shopping center and 300 timeshare apartments on the site, a 15-minute drive from the center of Panama City, she said.
Fort Amador, located at the entrance of the Panama Canal on the Pacific side, was turned over to Panamanian control last year.
Panama hopes to turn Fort Amador into its first cruise ship landing. Panama receives more than 250 cruise ships a year but they have no place to dock.
